newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS - U.S. crude imports ease, fueling API draw.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - U.S. crude imports ease, fueling API draw.

text.p: U.S. crude oil imports fell below normal levels last week, fueling a steep draw in crude inventories at Gulf Coast refineries and injecting some bullish sentiment back into the futures market, analysts said on Tuesday.

Distillate stocks, meanwhile, showed signs of maintaining a long-overdue seasonal build expected to feed a bearish outlook on heating oil futures in the coming weeks, analysts said following release of the weekly American Petroleum Institute petroleum products inventory estimates.

"Crude imports have been running at very, very high levels the last few weeks, and it's only a matter of time when you have to back off those high levels," said Tom Bentz, analyst with ING Futures and Options Inc in New York.

After maintaining a more than eight million barrel a week clip for the past few weeks, crude oil imports last week fell to 6.73 million barrels, down an average 1.65 million barrels a day and below the benchmark seven million barrels a week.
The drop in imports translated directly into a 4.22 million barrel draw in crude stocks on hand at PADD III Gulf Coast refineries for the week ended August 30, analysts said.

"In my opinion, the most bullish number in the API's this week is the crude, because the draw is all in PADD III. I expected to see most of that draw in the West Coast," said Dee Dee Finley, a Merrill Lynch energy broker in Kansas City, Mo.
The nation's refineries were operating at 94 percent of capacity, up 0.6 percentage points, with production shifting to increased distillate and decreased gasoline output.

Overall, distillate yields at U.S. refineries surveyed by the trade group rose to 23.9 percent from 22.5 percent and gasoline yields eased to 52.5 percent from 54.5 percent on the week, analysts said.

"The distillate build is a normal, seasonal build -- you could say it's even overdue," Bentz said. "If we do see several weeeks of builds, it could take some of the bullishness out of the heating oil market."
Distillate stocks on hand at U.S. refineries stood at 108.9 million barrels for the week, up 3.24 million barrels from the prior week but still 18.05 million barrels below the same week last year.
The distillate build was concentrated in the Midwest and Gulf Coasts, and stocks remained 14.97 million barrels below last year's levels on the East Coast.
Gasoline stocks were drawn down 3.71 million barrels nationwide, due largely to a 2.98 million barrel drop in stocks on hand at PADD II Midwest refineries, API said.
In the Midwest, strong prices fed by a flurry of refiner buying in late-August and early September prompted a surge in shipments into the region from Gulf Coast refiners.
NYMEX October crude oil was indicated higher at $23.24 a barrel bid, $23.34 asked in ACCESS after hours trade after closing off 16 cents at $23.24 in the floor session.
Front-month heating oil rose to $64.20 cents a gallon bid, 64.40 cents asked, while gasoline firmed to 63.31 cents a gallon, up 0.35 cent in early ACCESS trade.
